description.narrative: The Joint Initiative for Strategic Religious Action (JISRA) is a partnership between faith and non-faith based groups – including Christian, Islamic, interreligious and secular consortium partners and local partners – which will promote Freedom of Religion or Belief (FoRB) in Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iraq, Kenya, Mali, Nigeria and Uganda. The JISRA consortium consists of Mensen met een Missie, Search for Common Ground, Faith to Action Netowrk, and Tearfund (UK and NL). JISRA is funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs from 2021-2025

o Preparation of civil society shadow report with section on FoRB as a contribution to the Universal Periodic Review at the UN Human Rights Council o Lobby the EU on education laws and policies in Indonesia o 3 Engagements with the Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Women Empowerment and Child Protection o Religious moderation program initiated and implemented nationally by Ministry of Religious Affairs

description.narrative: Duty-bearers and decision-makers adopt, improve and implement religion and context-sensitive FoRB policies based on evidence and interaction with diverse religious actors and CSOs

comment.narrative: Baseline is 0 at the start of the programme

Lobbying has begun for implementation of law on handling FoRB-related conflict, and Action plan on women, peace and security. We have received some responses from the policy-makers, but no outcomes yet
o Regulations at the local level in Yogyakarta Special Region – Makassar and Manado
Baseline is 0 at the start of the programme

Developed a Universal Periodic Review shadow report reviewed by the UN Human Rights Commission in Geneva, Lobby on to revoke the Anti-Ahmadi Decree, to amend the Joint Ministerial Decree No. 1/2006 and allow bilding houses of worshop,

o Presidential Law (PNPS) Act Number 1 of 1965 needs to be rescinded because it restricts FoRB o Adoption of National Constitution (UUD) 1945 article 27 verse 1 about equal rights before the law o Adoption of National Constitution (UUD) 1945 article 29 verse 2 about freedom of religion or belief o Adoption of National Regulation (UU) No 7 1984; about convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women o Adoption of National Regulation (UU) No 29, 1999 and no 40 2008 about international convention on the elimination of all forms of racial discrimination o Adoption of National Regulation (UU) No 39 article 22, 1999 about human rights o Adoption of National Regulation (UU) article 18 No 12, 2005 about civil rights and politics.
Baseline is 0 at the start of the programme

Lobbying has begun for implementation of law on handling FoRB-related conflict, and Action plan on women, peace and security. We have received some responses from the policy-makers, but no outcomes yet

Instructions of the Governor of Special Region of Yogyakarta (DIY) concerning Prevention of Potential Social Conflicts o Draft Regulation of the Governor of DIY on Managing and Interpreting Differences in Schools
Baseline is 0 at the start of the programme

The govt adopted recommendations put forward through the UPR; KUPI II forum adopted recommendations on FGM. Lobby for the amendment of the regulation on the building houses of worship, revoke the Anti-Ahmadi decree, adoption of a policy to prevent violence, increase tolerance, and joint response on FORB by the UN special rapporteur has been on, but results are to be seen in the future, and require follow up.

o The Joint Decree of the Minister of Religion, the Attorney General, and the Minister of Home Affairs of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3 of 2008 to be rescinded or improved because it prohibits activities of the Ahmadiyyah community o The Joint Decree of the Minister of Religion and the Minister of Home Affairs number 8 & 9 of 2006 concerning Guidelines for Implementing the Duties of Regional Heads / Deputy Regional Heads in Maintaining Religious Harmony, Empowering Forum for Religious Harmony, and Establishing Places of Worship needs to be improved to facilitate the FoRB rights of citizens and ensure these rights do not violate public interest
